implementation_notes: The modern equivalent of CPS plus trampolining: the compiler builds the continuation-passing state machine, and returning a coroutine_handle from await_suspend makes the resume a tail call, so a chain of N steps occupies O(1) stack instead of O(N).
pitfalls: A void-returning await_suspend grows the stack by one frame per synchronous completion.
Sharing a handle across threads without release/acquire synchronisation is a data race.

variants.name: std::function continuation parameter
variants.implementation_notes: The direct hand-written CPS form in C++: the continuation is a std::function taking the result. Simple to read and to compose, but every continuation is a type-erased heap object.
variants.code_sketch: void repeat(int n, const std::function<void()>& k) { if (n == 0) k(); else repeat(n - 1, k); }
pitfalls: Capturing by reference past the call's lifetime dangles.
